1) the intraoperative frozen section analysis of sentinel node is a reliable method for detecting occult lymph node metastases in patients with squamous cell carcinoma of oral cavity and oropharynx, and 2) the accuracy of the intraoperative frozen sections is comparable to that of permanent sections.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the accuracy of FS is high enough to be used in the intraoperative setting for the detection of occult lymph node metastases in the SN biopsy procedure in OSCC.
frozen section of SNs is not accurate enough for intraoperative decision making in oral cavity cancer patients.
the intraoperative FS for detection of occult SN‐metastases in oral and oropha-ryngeal SCC is a reliable and accurate diagnostic tool with a high negative predictive value.
The main takeaway from our work is that
FS is a valid and reliable method in the detection of SN‐positivity in oral and orpharyngeal squamo‐cell carcinoma.
FS is a valid tool for the intraoperative assessment of SNs in OSCC and can be used as a reliable method to guide further treatment.
the intraoperative FS of SNs for oral cavity cancer is an accurate method for detection of metastases and can be a useful tool for the management of the N‐stage in these patients.
